newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Media shake-up talk pushes Seven to record.
newsitem.headline: Media shake-up talk pushes Seven to record.

text.p: Share in television broadcaster Seven Network Ltd hit a record high on reports that the government was close to finalising its new media ownership laws, which could see Rupert Murdoch up his stake in Seven.
At 3.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), Seven shares were 15 cents or 2.88 percent up at A$5.35 with more than 560,000 shares traded.
"There has been a pretty solid market in them in recent times and those reports this morning just add some spice to it," said dealer Jamie Spiteri of Shaw Stockbroking.
Australian newspapers reported that the new laws would allow Kerry Packer and Rupert Murdoch expand their empires.

The plan would allow a single proprietor to own one newspaper and one television station in the major cities of Sydney and Melbourne and would raise foreign ownership limits to 25 percent from 15 percent.
The plan would clear the way for Packer, Australia's richest man, to take over newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd and for Murdoch's News Corp to increase its shareholding in the Seven Network.
News Corp currently owns 15 percent of Seven, while Seven's chairman Kerry Stokes owns 26 percent of the network and has said he wants to raise his stake to 30 percent.
